subject: [PATCH v4 0/2] mm/vmscan: reduce lru_lock contention via vmstat-derived scan-balance cost

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that exposing userspace counters for anon/file reclaim work has diagnostic value, but doesn't have a concrete usecase and wants to avoid creating another hidden lruvec rstat infrastructure. They proposed modifying the existing node.c code to make PGROTATE_ANON and PGROTATE_FILE public.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that there is still one outstanding comment from Shakeel, but otherwise considers the review process complete and plans to finalize the patch in the next week.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks Andrew! Yes I think we have the reviews, but just 1 outstanding
comment from Shakeel and need to shorten commit message as Johannes
mentioned. Hopefully we will have a final version next week.

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the new counters can be almost fully derived from existing counters, specifically dPGSCAN_ANON, dPGSTEAL_ANON, and dPGDEACTIVATE_ANON, which capture the necessary information for understanding reclaim behavior. The reviewer suggested splitting dPGDEACTIVATE_ANON by type and stopping its count or having a separate event for MADV_COLD driven deactivations.
reviews.raw_body:
Hm, this is an interesting discussion.

The existing PGROTATED is kind of useless. When it's bumped:

- truncation fails and moves folios to the LRU tail for faster reclaim
- writeback ends on folio that was tried to reclaim, moves to LRU tail for fast retry

Ok, who needs to know this? The new counters you're adding, on the
other hand, they capture the information you frequently need for
understanding reclaim behavior.

That said, looking closer at this one more time, you can already
(almost) derive them fully from existing counters:

drotated = (dPGSCAN_ANON - dPGSTEAL_ANON) + dPGDEACTIVATE_ANON

The first two are already split by anon and file. The third you'd have
to (1) split by type and (2) stop counting, or have a separate event,
for MADV_COLD driven deactivations.

And (2) seems overdue anyway. There is no point in maintaining counts
for what userspace madvises. And it adds noise when it gets conflated
with a stat tracking kernel reclaim behavior.

2026-07-24.patch_summary: This patch reduces contention on the lru_lock by moving the calculation of scan-balance costs from producers to consumers, using vmstat-derived counters instead of scalar values in struct lruvec. The patch introduces a dedicated cost_lock for per-lruvec accumulation and decay, improving the accuracy of the cost model across reclaim gaps.
